content: Prisma connection pool exhaustion: most common cause is instantiating a new PrismaClient per request instead of a singleton reused across the app/process. In containerized/multi-instance deployments (e.g. PM2 cluster, multiple replicas), each instance holds its own pool, so total connections = instances × pool size, easily exceeding Postgres max_connections. For a redirect-hot-path service, recommend PgBouncer in transaction pooling mode in front of Postgres so many short-lived redirect lookups share a small number of real backend connections; keep Prisma's own connection_limit conservative per instance.
